question: When do two conditioned distinctions become equivalent?

disposition.summary: Two conditioned distinctions may be treated as equivalent only when the declared equivalence relation preserves typed class, conditioning lineage, admissibility context, directional order, and non-collapse. Equivalence is not identity and must not alias distinct conditioned classes.

formal_scaffold.candidate_condition: CondEq(<a>_b,<c>_d) holds only if TypeClassCompatible, LineageComparable, AdmCtxComparable, OrderCompatible, ResidueNonAlias, and NonCollapse all hold.
preservation_requirements: Both operands are typed conditioned distinctions.
The comparison relation is explicitly declared.
Conditioning lineage is comparable and recoverable.
Admissibility context is comparable and recoverable.
Directional order is preserved or an explicit lawful symmetry condition is declared.
Typed residue and conditioned class labels are not aliased.
Equivalence is kept distinct from process identity.
formal_scaffold.exclusion_rule: Equivalence is inadmissible if it erases conditioning context, reverses order without declaration, aliases distinct classes, collapses typed residue, or is read as identity.

failure_conditions: Conditioning lineage is erased or not comparable.
Admissibility context is erased or not comparable.
Directional order is reversed without an explicit lawful symmetry declaration.
Distinct conditioned classes or typed residues are aliased.
Equivalence is treated as process identity or physical identity.

remaining_work: Convert the campaign-supported equivalence scaffold into a formal proof artifact if theorem promotion is requested.
Run independent rigor endorsement before raising the conditioning induction ceiling.
Audit equivalence uses for identity collapse or context erasure.
Keep OQ_COND_004 and OQ_COND_005 separately tracked until each Appendix F item is synchronized.

does_not_prove: That distinct conditioned classes may be aliased.
Physical identity, physical equivalence, or causal equivalence.
